newsitem.title: USA: 1996 cobalt demand, supply should increase - CDI.
newsitem.headline: 1996 cobalt demand, supply should increase - CDI.

text.p: Although the cobalt market has been facing a recent softening of prices and increased supply, cobalt demand and supply should increase this year over 1995 levels, officials of the Cobalt Development Insitute (CDI) said Wednesday.

Officials made their comments at a one-day CDI meeting in Pittsburgh. Ed Keilty, CDI official and a member of the Defense Logistics Agency's (DLA) market advisory committee, said demand for all cobalt grades is expected to increase this year from last year but an estimated number was not yet available.
Demand last year totaled about 24,000 tons.
Keilty also said cobalt supply is expected to increase this year by 10 to 12 percent. Supply last year totaled about 26,000 tons.
Meanwhile, DLA officials said at the meeting they should be able to meet their sales goal of $81 million for the current fiscal year even if cobalt sales wane.

Richard Connelly, DLA administrator, said the agency can reach its sales goal without cobalt by selling the eight other commodities it was authorized to begin selling in fiscal 1997, including platinum, palladium and tantalum.
The agency's current fiscal year began October 1 and ends September 30, 1997.
"This goal ($81 million in sales) is easily achievable," Connelly said. "But if market conditions dictate, we won't sell any cobalt."
Prices for low-grade cobalt have softened and currently are hovering in a range of $19 to $20 per pound, after beginning the calendar year at around $28 per pound.

The DLA was authorized to sell six million pounds of low-grade cobalt in fiscal 1997. Its plan is to sell three million pounds of low-grade cobalt on a sealed bid basis and another three million pounds on a negotiated bid basis.
The agency sold four million pounds on a negotiated bid basis in fiscal 1996.
Connelly said sealed bids for cobalt will be accepted in December, March 1997 and May 1997. Negotiated bids will be accepted in February, April and September of next year.
